{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUhdMr88AAAABUF8vRA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlJVizg9nq_s", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlJVi", "number": 100, "title": "Sync task Issues and AI execution permission with shared Project via GitHub Actions", "body": "## Problem

The shared user Project [ProjectWeave + GitWeave](https://github.com/users/takahirox/projects/4) tracks work across `takahirox/projectweave` and `takahirox/gitweave`. The account's built-in auto-add workflow limit prevents configuring both repositories. Implement automatic Issue addition and synchronization of AI execution permission from Issue state and labels with GitHub Actions in this repository; the other repository has a separate task. Eligible Issues should become executable automatically by ProjectWeave's continuously running `coordinate` mode, without a separate manual Ready step.

## Required behavior

Add this repository's Issues to Project #4 when they match:

```text
is:issue is:open label:task -label:draft
```

- Handle Issue creation, reopening, closing, label addition, and label removal. In particular, removing `draft` from an open Issue with `task` must add it and make it Ready.
- For an open Issue with `task` and without `draft`, ensure it belongs to Project #4 and set `AI execution = Ready` automatically. Re-adding `task` or removing `draft` restores Ready when the full condition matches.
- Set Status to `Todo` for a newly created Project item or an existing eligible item with no Status, so ProjectWeave can select it. Preserve any already-set Status (`Todo`, `In Progress`, or `Done`), including on repeated matching events and reopening. Do not reset running or finished work to Todo.
- Repeated matching events must not create duplicate Project items. Apart from synchronizing `AI execution` and initializing an unset Status, preserve existing Project field values, including Priority.
- If `task` is removed, `draft` is added, or the Issue is closed, set `AI execution = Not ready` for an already-registered Project #4 item. Retain its Project membership and preserve its Status; the built-in Issue-closed workflow handles the closure Status separately. Never add a noneligible Issue just to set Not ready. Ignore pull requests.
- Closing an Issue already in the Project should result in `Done` through GitHub's standard Issue-closed Project workflow. Document checking that this built-in workflow is enabled. Do not create a Project item for an unregistered closed Issue, remove its existing Project item, or infer that every closure means implemented work: the Issue's `Completed` / `Not planned` reason distinguishes those outcomes.
- The Actions workflow updates Project state only. ProjectWeave's `coordinate` process is responsible for executing open, Todo, Ready Tasks under its resource policy. Do not launch AI directly from Actions or introduce a `Pending` Status.
- No automatic backfill of existing Issues is required.

## Scope boundary

Changing `AI execution` to `Not ready` prevents future ProjectWeave task admission; it does not stop an already-running execution. Stopping running work, checking eligibility before merge, and passing Project execution permission into GitWeave are deferred to future work. Do not implement them here. Project state belongs to ProjectWeave; GitWeave should not start reading Project state as part of this task.

## Implementation and authentication

Add a small workflow under `.github/workflows/` using the GitHub GraphQL `addProjectV2ItemById` API for additions and `updateProjectV2ItemFieldValue` for Ready/Not ready synchronization and Todo initialization (GitHub CLI is available on hosted Ubuntu runners). Target user `takahirox`, Project #4. Locate existing items, Status, and the `AI execution` field without assuming they are on the first API page. Reconcile against the Issue's current state and labels so delayed or concurrent label events do not restore stale permission. Use the Issue's node ID without interpolating Issue titles or bodies into shell code. Avoid checking out or executing repository code for this automation.

Use the Actions repository secret `ADD_TO_PROJECT_PAT`. The ordinary `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot access Projects. Document how the owner creates an expiring personal access token with the required user-Project write permission (a classic PAT with `project` scope is a documented option for this public-repository setup) and registers the secret in **both** repositories. Do not create, retrieve, expose, commit, or repurpose existing credentials. Secret provisioning is a separate owner action; state clearly that automation is inactive until it is configured. Report a missing secret with an actionable message.

Follow this repository's Issue → PR → review development flow. Keep changes limited to this workflow and concise setup documentation.

## Acceptance and verification

- Validate workflow syntax and the eligibility condition.
- Verify the addition condition matrix: open+task; open+task+draft; open without task; closed+task; removing draft; and repeated matching events.
- Verify eligible Issues become Ready automatically, new/unset-Status items become Todo, and already-set Status and Priority are preserved. Re-adding task and removing draft must restore Ready when eligible.
- Verify removing `task`, adding `draft`, or closing registered Issues makes them Not ready and preserves membership. Label changes on registered `Todo`, `In Progress`, and `Done` items must preserve Status. Noneligible unregistered Issues must not be added. Check idempotency and delayed/concurrent event handling.
- Verify/document the built-in Issue-closed workflow's `Done` behavior and confirm no `Pending` field option, running-work cancellation, or merge gate was introduced.
- Document a live verification procedure after secret provisioning, including confirming that an eligible Issue appears once in Project #4.
- Record validation performed and any live checks blocked by the missing secret in the PR.

## References

- https://docs.github.com/en/issues/planning-and-tracking-with-projects/automating-your-project/automating-projects-using-actions
- https://docs.github.com/en/issues/planning-and-tracking-with-projects/automating-your-project/using-the-api-to-manage-projects
